newsitem.title: USA: Vivus fall on misreading of news - analyst.
newsitem.headline: Vivus fall on misreading of news - analyst.

text.p: Shares of VIVUS Inc fell sharply Monday after some investors misread the company's news about a temporary reduction in shipments, one analysts who follows the company said. Vivus shares were off 8-1/8 to 40.

The company, which makes a treatment to correct male impotence, announced it would reduce shipments through April 10 because its staff had been diverted by a Food and Drug Adminstration inspection that turned up certain deficiencies.
However, PaineWebber analyst Charles Olsziewski said those deficiencies were most likely minor and would not have an impact on long term production.

"Based on the conversations I've had today, people have totally misread the facts," Olsziewski said. "People think the production slowdown relates to the deficiencies turned up in the FDA inspection and that couldn't be further from the truth. The truth is that during the FDA inspection a lot of people were diverted (from normal duties), so while production was still going on, the product has been stockpiling."
"I would think that 98 percent of inspections come up with deficiencies," he said, adding that they were usually minor.
Olsziewski said he expects Vivus will "quite handily" exceed his first quarter sales and earnings forecasts.
For the first quarter, which ends March 31, Olsziewski had forecast Vivus would reprt $19 million in product revenue and net income of $0.25 per share, numbers which he now says are too low.
Vivus representatives were not immediately available for comment.
